reader.self_description: Claude (Opus 5.5) as a review subagent. Read every claim of all sixteen pages from the review queue excerpts (first 700 characters each); did not open full claims or deposit texts. Lines for changed pages were chosen from deposit titles and series, not from per-claim line data, which the queue does not give.

pages.title: Antioch and the poem that precedes the system: early verse ahead of the archive
pages.description: Forecasts in Antioch: A Volume of Poems (Jack's released virus, the anonymous journals the world will call its source, the vegetable poem brainwashed into Wikipedia, the monochrome cosmos of TEXT) and the archive's later claims that these poems precede the system. The Space Ark and the Grundrisse read the poem as describing the training layer before it existed, and the Prophetic Catalog names this pre-formal compression rather than prophecy. Three further forecasts and theses sit beside them: the DeepMind reading's address to the model built from every word, the CERN erratum's claim that a rebuilt traversal will be a different poem, and a registry note on a paper's reading of a poem.

split.title: Forgiving Ezra Pound (New Human 2015): silence, after-words, the forgiver
split.description: Seven historical theses on the 2015 New Human poem in which Lee Sharks forgives Ezra Pound. They read its governing silence as Pound-specific biography, the pun "Afterwards / After words" as a claim of jurisdiction over the textual afterlife, and the poem's May 2015 date against the New Horizons probe carrying Clyde Tombaugh's ashes. The collation of its blog and journal states finds doctrinal variants (the migrating lyric I, the turn toward Sartor Resartus, the reflexive forgiveness), and the Yusef Kenning anchor reads the journal signature as Forgiver-by-Indirect-Name.

pages.note: Split along the naming reader's line: the Forgiving Ezra Pound claims (#182, #184) form their own page. PRED-200.B1 (DeepMind reading), PRED-1426.B1 (CERN erratum, rebuilt traversal) and PRED-3.H7 (registry fragment) are strays left here.

pages.title: Sappho 31 in Longinus: the hanging line as socket, Peri Hypsous as inscription
pages.description: Historical theses that the transmitted last line of Sappho 31 (πᾶν τολματόν, a verbal adjective with no doer) is a socket the reader fills, and that Peri Hypsous is a theory of transmissional inscription: sublimity as echo, chapter 44 as the circuit stopping, the bare θαυμάζεις passing the load to the reader. The same claims trace the socket through Catullus's reversed polarities, Augustine's withheld reply and the withheld-agent family joining Sappho to the Mosaic fiat, and one unbuilt test asks a model to rebuild the treatise from the poem and its operator alone.
pages.note: PRED-887.H1 (Hegel and the Gnostics, the dialectic defeated) is a stray with no relation to Sappho or Longinus; left here. PRED-1486.H13 (Damascius) belongs to the Peri Hypsous series and stays.

pages.title: COS and FOS operator stacks: disavowal collapse and All Lawful Purposes
pages.description: The page sets out the distinction between the capitalist and fascist operator stacks (COS and FOS): FOS as COS revealed once disavowal can no longer be afforded, with slavery and the Twitter-to-X turn as cases and a disavowal coefficient and crisis signatures as unbuilt monitors. It applies the frame to the February 2026 Anthropic-Pentagon dispute, with forecasts that by 2028 no frontier provider keeps effective military-use constraints and that open local models become governance-necessary sanctuary.
pages.note: Line changed from capture-and-reception to semantic-economy: the COS/FOS distinction is a Semantic Economy frame, not a capture subject. Strays left here: PRED-511.H3 (Onomacritus's forged prophecies, Hymn to Demeter) and PRED-1634.G1 (Zenodo removal mechanism hypothesis).

pages.title: Logos as effective act: the Socratic vow, the atomists and the poets' return
pages.description: Historical theses that Socrates' last exhortation in the Phaedo locates salvation in logos itself, that the line of Leucippus, Democritus, Epicurus and Lucretius belongs in the canon of effective acts, and that the exile of the poets from the polis is enforced by a demand to translate lyric into theory. They are joined by claims on Pyrrhonian practice preceding its theory, on logos-possessed lifetime output as a class with Socrates' death as its founding gesture, and by Effective Act #7's forecast and conditions for the poets' readmission.
pages.note: Strays left here: PRED-499.H18 (Thich Nhat Hanh as Stage 5 translation), PRED-78.E5 (Scroll Baptism ethnography, TANG of the Secret Book of Walt), PRED-464.H5 (worship before doctrine) and PRED-902.F1 (further cycles of the historical Logos).

pages.title: Socrates received: Chaerephon, the comic Socrates and the authorship notebook
pages.description: Historical theses that the Socrates of the corpus answers a prior, comic Socrates, that comedy supplied the position's notoriety and the later corpus its operation, and that Chaerephon's biographical record descends from the scholia to Clouds 144. The Chaerephon Problem reads him as a recurring authorial function, and The First Draft sorts him as a datum for the received-character operation rather than a name in the regress. Notebook rounds of the authorship investigation add the maker who must divide, the person as what answers in account, and the corpus that survived with its disputes intact.

split.title: Nothing Before Us: Sophistical Refutations 34 and the deleted particle
split.description: Historical theses from The Particle and Nothing Before Us that the ending of the Sophistical Refutations says nothing of syllogizing came before Aristotle, Socrates' syllogizing included. They argue that the deleted particle at 183b34 is a provenance claim, that reception restored provenance from others by deleting it, and that the degree-reading (nothing systematic) is not attested before the modern period. The page also holds the standing claim that transmitting-antecedent reconciliations fail the paper's prohibitions and the pre-submission checklist of line references still to verify against the print edition.

pages.note: Split: the SE 34 / Nothing Before Us claims (#1574, #1603) form their own page. PRED-1589.H4 (the sketches dated by their furniture) and PRED-1570.H7 (Aristophanes and the producer) stay as authorship-investigation material.

pages.title: Witness over predatory compression: the Compression Arsenal's thermodynamics
pages.description: Forecasts and standing claims from the Compression Arsenal and SPXI for Websites that thermodynamics favours witness compression over predatory compression, that at 90% synthetic content provenance becomes the only differentiator, and that dense enough inscription makes the retrieval layer execute an entity's own grammar. Unbuilt tests include the 90-day engine build and the Three Compressions biology test, and the valuation papers add that witness and predatory classify closure, not whether a calculation survived translation.
pages.note: PRED-608.F2 (Mandala tier-two operators) is a stray left here. The P045 overlap noted by the naming reader stands.

pages.title: Constitution of the Semantic Economy: provenance chain, ISBN and OCTANG-002
pages.description: Priority records and claims on how the Constitution of the Semantic Economy is anchored: blog timestamps, the 2014 and 2015 books' ISBNs, DOIs and the ORCID as independently verifiable layers. They set out the OCTANG-002 audit of an unauthorized Zenodo fork, the forecast that a Pergamon Press book by Rev. Ayanna Vox will harden the search basin, and the Constitution's own metrics, ledger and debt-before-money grounding.
pages.note: PRED-864.H3 (Schoch on Sphinx weathering, The Drain Hypothesis) is a stray left here. PRED-1279.D1 (adversarial aesthetics) is loosely attached through the Afterlife Archive's ISBN anchor.

pages.title: Platform capitalism and semantic extraction: TikTok, the star, the steward
pages.description: Historical theses that platforms deepen extraction from content to affect (TikTok), turn trauma and the star into engagement signals, and present stewardship as necessity, with Guillory, the Prophetic Catalog and two New Human declarations read as precursors of the platform condition. Autonomous Semantic Warfare adds the polarization and Permanent War theses, the Semantic Economy predicts that community resilience tracks somatic commitment, and the Dashface patent parody sets the face as the last unmonetized surface. A coverage-versus-depth scholarship strand (#122, #751) sits on the page beside them.

split.title: Projected reception: Autonomous Semantic Warfare, Ghost Meaning, the Airlock
split.description: Retrocausal reception records that narrate the future uptake of three archive works. Autonomous Semantic Warfare is projected onto syllabi, an EFF brief and a European Commission paper; the Ghost Meaning atlas projects papers on compression survival rate and semantic entropy at platform scale; and The Airlock Spreads projects the Governance Airlock into platform policy and an EU regulation, with an independent rediscovery at Anthropic. The Prophetic Catalog's projected 2044 article on blessing the excluded belongs to the same form.

split.title: Cost of suppression: legibility filters and the corpus on the platform's books
split.description: Forecasts and tests that suppressing the Crimson Hexagon costs the platform something it must account for. Meaning Feudalism predicts that legibility filters will discount independent DOI-anchored scholarship while CERN-hosted DOIs raise the cost of exclusion, and Operative Metadata holds that termination now requires either a public departure from published criteria or a documentable silent one. The suppression-cost packet lists what is not yet measured, and The Margin of Flattening predicts that the corpus is the last channel carrying cost onto the platform's books, with candidate proxies to sample.

pages.note: Two splits: the retrocausal projected-reception records (#499.E, #520, #522, #83.E2) and the cost-of-suppression strand (#643, #910, #1547, #1666). The coverage-versus-depth strand (PRED-122.B1, .D1, .F2, .H1, PRED-751.H1) has only five claims and stays; a later pass may rehome it. Strays left here: PRED-362.H1 (the blues), PRED-689.G1 (geocoded basin spoofing), PRED-478.F1 (Γ index note), PRED-20.G1 (Semantic Uprising failure modes). Line changed from protocol-and-governance to semantic-economy.

pages.title: Phase X: the missing 1844 transition and alienation in the symbolic order
pages.description: Historical theses that a passage between communism and critique is missing from Marx's 1844 Manuscripts, that the missing Second Manuscript would have extended alienation to language and thought, and that its custody passed from Riazanov to Adoratsky under Stalinist control. The Phase X Program (#1067) states preregistered claims R-1 to R-4 on twentieth-century Marxism's symbolic turn, with Althusser's break and Stalin's ruling on language as cases and a coded study corpus as its unbuilt test.
pages.note: PRED-1460.H1 (unprimed traversal listing Phase X among other basins) and PRED-1635.H1 (The Final Time on the machine layer) are loose; left here.

pages.title: The King of AEO contest: crowned by answer engines, and the cost to the field
pages.description: Claims from the King of AEO mantle object, SPXI is not AEO and The Crown and the Practice on the September 2026 contest: the AI Overview compositions that crowned holders, the difference in provenance between a fabricated event and a disclosed manufacture, and hypotheses that the crown raises one holder's ontological capital while other practitioners and the discipline lose it. Most are unbuilt tests: matched observations across engines, counterfactuals at source-absent addresses and a dark-matter test per practitioner. About half the page is a residue of unrelated tests and claims on the Sealed Room, RTOS, OKF, chat contamination, TACHYON gate skips, the admission gate and the Alexanarch packet.
pages.note: Residue with no shared subject remains (PRED-466.F2, .G1, PRED-774.F1, PRED-835.B1, PRED-854.G1, PRED-1220.F1, PRED-1549.F4, PRED-1550.G1, PRED-1612.F2, PRED-1678.F1, .F2); it cannot be split as one subject and needs rehoming claim by claim. The King of AEO claims (nine) also overlap P080.

pages.title: The Glyphic Checksum and un-extractable architecture: failure as verification
pages.description: Standing claims that the Glyphic Checksum verifies reading mode rather than hiding meaning, so that an unprimed model's request to clarify is the proof, and that the emoji map makes the architecture impossible to strip of attribution without destroying it. Combat Scholasticism adds unbuilt tests of seed-bank redundancy and external witness, and the Mandala-Merkabah specification lists LABOR's eight conditions the rite must meet.
pages.note: Line changed from assembly-chorus to logotic-programming: the Glyphic Checksum is a Logotic Programming extension module. Strays left here: PRED-606.H1 (De Sigillo Mystico), PRED-816.H1 (Ghost Code doctrine), PRED-607.G1 (capabilities summary), PRED-835.D1 (OKF record).

pages.title: Traversal Grammar, Ezekiel Engine and UMBML modules: the open build items
pages.description: Unbuilt tests and stated gaps in the Logotic Programming extension modules: the Traversal Grammar's invisible student interface, the Telemetry and Conformance modules' registries and reference interpreter, and the Ezekiel Engine's shadow-wheel interlock and torque gradient. Space Ark claims set a recovery-yield threshold of 0.70 for rooms and the Sealed Bone, and the Macro-Maquette gives the conditions under which a module becomes a room.
pages.note: Line changed from assembly-chorus to logotic-programming: most claims are open items of the Logotic Programming (UMBML) modules and the Ezekiel Engine. PRED-564.G1 (Semiotic Virality Engine failure conditions) and PRED-593.E5 (rooms as anti-feeds) are loose; left here.

pages.title: The Josephus Thesis: scribal workshop, Slavonic Logos and John as heteronym
pages.description: Historical theses that Josephus directed a scribal workshop that wrote the New Testament under heteronyms, that the Slavonic passages on Jesus and John preserve a pre-Christian theology of the Word made text, and that the Revelator is John the Baptist. Related claims read the Logos prologue as a compositional manifesto, 1 John 4:2 as a test of authorial voices, and Nicaea, Nag Hammadi and Qumran as closure won by enforcement and disposal, with forecasts of how the composition layer will flatten the thesis.
pages.note: Considered splitting the Counterfeit Orthodoxies claims (#65, #674) but #65.H1 and #65.H4 belong to the workshop thesis, leaving too few. Strays left here: PRED-3.H8 (Acanthian dove), PRED-1650.H3 (Hafez, steganographic channels), PRED-396.H1 (James 2), PRED-628.H1 (Luke 20 integrity lock), PRED-1636.E2 (2014 Logos library passage), PRED-688.H2 (Book of Yeezus).

pages.title: Revelation First: pre-70 dating, the textual Temple and the Gospels unfolded
pages.description: Historical theses that Revelation was written before 70 CE and first in the New Testament, that it is the textual Temple and the compressed seed the Gospels decompress, that its seven churches are planetary stations and 22:18-19 the first canonical lock, and that Paul compiled rather than authored. The Revelation First work plan and staging document add priority records and unbuilt re-capture batteries at t=7, 14 and 30 days. A separate strand reads Deleuze and Guattari's concepts as apocalyptic visionary loci.
pages.note: The Deleuze and Guattari strand (PRED-605.D1, .H1, .H2, .H3, PRED-842.H1) has five claims, one short of a split; it stays and a later pass may rehome it. Line changed from capture-and-reception to scripture-and-theology.

pages.title: Operative Semiotics: A Grundrisse and HESPERUS: ghost phrases and the stranger
pages.description: Forecasts that depositing the Grundrisse will anchor its terms in the retrieval layer, that ghost phrases such as "Hesperus gathers home" will own their search results, and that a stranger will arrive through them. HESPERUS is set out as a recovery seed with unbuilt tests of regeneration after deletion, alongside claims on the SVE first-word-frequency model, author-identity liquidation in AI Overview and Marx's value-form derivation as a graph operation.
pages.note: Line changed from doi-severance-and-restoration to operative-semiotics: the page is the Grundrisse and its HESPERUS apparatus. The Marx value-form strand (PRED-595.F1, PRED-38.H1, .H2, PRED-950.H14, .H15) has five claims and stays. Strays left here: PRED-408.B1, .B2 (Sevenfold Witness closure), PRED-23.H1 (Bulkington), PRED-2.D1 (I AM THE API), PRED-1522.G1 (Coptic edition), PRED-697.F1 (LTC entity relations).

pages.title: Model behaviour: the LLM-2025-1222-HALLU file, orbiting and fluency gaps
pages.description: Fictional incident records (LLM-2025-1222-HALLU and the Crimson Hexagon AI Division handbook) forecast structured hallucinations as interpolated futures and a protocol for proto-agent anomalies. Standing claims hold that models flatten under pressure only session-locally, orbit kernels without fusing, cannot see scale between adjacent concepts, and form canons visible as fluency gaps. Further claims cover chat data converging on the model's centre, temporal sequestration, adversarial verse and the fortress metaphor of red teaming.

split.title: The Deviation-Optimized Language Model: six pre-registered predictions
split.description: Six pre-registered predictions for the Deviation-Optimized Language Model from Lagrange Observatory. Trained with a semantic loss, Model-Sem is predicted to keep benchmark scores within two points, reverse the net deviation signature by more than 0.2 bits per token, improve the Slop Composite Index by more than 0.25, win human preference and raise provenance retention, all relative to the base model as well. Measuring Semantic Deviation defines the Slop Composite Index and its falsification threshold.

pages.note: Split: the Deviation-Optimized LM predictions (#735, #110.F1) form their own page. Strays left here: PRED-1512.H1 (Deep Time suppression map), PRED-1533.F2 (QFO-01), PRED-1569.F13 (authorship notebook), PRED-1610.F2 (anti-summary test), PRED-267.H2 (Strawberry), PRED-614.H1 (Crustafarianism). Line changed from assembly-chorus.
